name: Lizard

modes.label: Sandbox measured usage (4 vCPU / 4 GiB fixed template)
modes.note: Measured usage, not reservation; exact RAM statistic undocumented. Reject requested RAM >4 GiB; not a valid 4/8 quote. Snapshot retention unsupported; paused state resides in host memory.

plans.name: Pro PAYG
plans.note: Account capacity limits unpublished; enterprise terms custom.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom contract adds custom replica limits, SOC 2/HIPAA compliance, SSO/SAML, RBAC/audit log, SLA support and dedicated nodes on demand. Sandbox account concurrency is still not published.

caveats: Public sandbox API is fixed 4 vCPU / 4096 MiB; app quotas of 20 vCPU/40 GB do not establish sandbox sizing. Cannot serve a single 4 vCPU/8 GiB sandbox as documented.

Marketing advertises custom templates, snapshots and shared volumes; newer sandbox docs restrict create to base/code-interpreter-v1, single-attached node-local volumes and non-durable host-memory pause. Docs take precedence.
Pause/expiration lifecycle has a documented unresolved backend issue. Timeout may expire while paused; no guaranteed long-term retention.
Exact measured-memory accounting, minimum billing, payment processing fee and minimum top-up amount unpublished.
Concurrency capacity is account-limited but no verified numeric sandbox concurrency guarantee for 50 is published.
90 ms marketing cold-start claim differs from 200 ms llms index; neither is an independently measured benchmark.
No confirmed durable named user snapshots or public fork API; do not treat pause as backup.
Volume meter $0.141912/GiB per 730-hour month cannot be stored as snapshot_gib_month; retained VM snapshots are not offered.
Enterprise pricing absent; public mode only. Trial expires in 31 days.

Root filesystem size of a sandbox is not published; all requested disk is priced at the volume rate $0.000000054/GB/s (~$0.1419/GB-month) as an upper bound. Volumes are single-attached and node-local.

Purchased credits do not expire, but the $10 trial credit expires after 31 days. Auto top-up is optional. The minimum top-up and payment fee are only displayed inside the authenticated top-up screen and remain unknown.

When credit reaches zero, creation can be restricted and running services can pause after an unspecified grace period. The public page does not publish the grace duration or retention/deletion deadline.

Volumes are 1–50 GB by current public default, 5 GB default, one sandbox attachment at a time, node-local, and billed on used space rather than allocated size. The engine's requested-GB multiplication is therefore an upper bound for sparse volumes.

Dashboard sandboxes created manually have no timeout; SDK default is five minutes; raw API timeoutMs=0 means no expiration and the maximum explicit millisecond timeout is 2147483647. Commands do not reset lifetime.

Pro's advertised 20 vCPU/40 GB and 5 replicas apply to applications, not Sandbox size or account fleet capacity. Public Sandbox create remains fixed at 4 vCPU/4096 MiB, and the effective account cap must be obtained from the provider.

fleet.verification: Signup page determines whether payment method is required; published $10 trial credit does not prove no-card access.
fleet.notes: Limits docs explicitly warn not to equate app caps with sandbox capacity. Sandbox create shape 4 vCPU/4 GiB is not account total; advertised thousands parallel is not new-account quota. Ask provider for effective account cap before sizing any fleet.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: After it stops, only files written to an attached Persistent Volume at `/workspace` can be reused by a later sandbox.
snapshot_auto.note: Nothing is saved automatically on stop/expiry; lifetime is a fixed deadline, not an idle timer. Pause/resume return HTTP 501.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Pause, resume, fork, snapshot, restore, and file watching currently return HTTP 501.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Dashboard: 'Creating user snapshots, pausing, and resuming are not supported.' Marketing page: 'User-created snapshots are not available.'

harness_api.quote: | `sandbox.process.exec(cmd)` | Run a shell command; return stdout, stderr, and exitCode. |
harness_api.note: SDK surface is create/connect/list/getInfo, process.exec, fs.*, getHost, setTimeout, kill. A 'codex' template exists (harness preinstalled = agent_harnesses), but no API to drive it; command timeouts 1-600 s.

secret_proxy.quote: Create-time `envs` and `metadata` are also not applied.
secret_proxy.note: No credential proxy documented. The platform's secrets are env vars merged into app services' environments (docs/variables); for sandboxes even create-time env vars are not applied, so credentials have to be passed in via commands/files.

volume_attach.quote: A volume in Lizard (lizard.build) keeps data after a sandbox stops. It mounts at **`/workspace`** and attaches to **one sandbox at a time**.
volume_attach.note: Named node-local volumes 1-50 GB (default 5), billed on used space; attached at create; survive sandbox kill but not node loss.

volume_shared.quote: An attached volume cannot attach to another sandbox or be deleted.
volume_shared.note: Single attachment only (read-write). Managed S3 object storage exists as a platform addon but is not a sandbox mount.

docker_inside.quote: Sandboxes run short-lived commands and agent tasks in Kubernetes pods with the runc runtime. They share the host kernel; they are not Firecracker virtual machines.
docker_inside.note: Shared-kernel unprivileged runc pods; no docker-in-docker / privileged container support is documented anywhere in the sandbox docs.

nested_virt.quote: Sandboxes run short-lived commands and agent tasks in Kubernetes pods with the runc runtime. They share the host kernel; they are not Firecracker virtual machines.
nested_virt.note: Shared-kernel container runtime, not a VM/microVM; no /dev/kvm or nested-virtualization capability is offered or documented.

desktop.quote: Sandboxes: Kubernetes environments with a shared host kernel for agent commands and files; attach a volume at /workspace for persistent files, set a lifetime, and stop each sandbox after use
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — sandboxes only expose process exec, file I/O, and an HTTPS port; no VNC/RDP/desktop stream exists.

browser.quote: Sandboxes: Kubernetes environments with a shared host kernel for agent commands and files; attach a volume at /workspace for persistent files, set a lifetime, and stop each sandbox after use
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Lizard Studio is a Chrome extension for inspecting a locally-run app, not a managed/remote browser inside the sandbox.

computer_use.quote: Sandboxes: Kubernetes environments with a shared host kernel for agent commands and files
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no screenshot/click driving API exists; the SDK only offers process.exec and fs.*.

anti_bot.quote: Sandboxes run short-lived commands and agent tasks in Kubernetes pods with the runc runtime.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a command/file execution sandbox has no browser stealth/fingerprinting feature.

captcha_solving.quote: Sandboxes run short-lived commands and agent tasks in Kubernetes pods with the runc runtime.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no browser/CAPTCHA feature is offered by this command-execution sandbox platform.

egress_ip_type.quote: Sandboxes run short-lived commands and agent tasks in Kubernetes pods with the runc runtime.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: multi-tenant Kubernetes cluster egress; no residential/mobile or static/dedicated IP feature is documented anywhere.

fork.quote: Pause, resume, fork, snapshot, restore, and file watching currently return HTTP 501.
fork.note: Fork API exists in name but is unimplemented (HTTP 501) on the current runtime.

fork_running.quote: Pause, resume, fork, snapshot, restore, and file watching currently return HTTP 501.
fork_running.note: Fork itself is unavailable (HTTP 501), so cloning a running sandbox is not possible.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Pause, resume, fork, snapshot, restore, and file watching currently return HTTP 501.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No fork/snapshot capability at all, so no memory-preserving fork exists.

wake_on_request.quote: Pause, resume, fork, snapshot, restore, and file watching currently return HTTP 501.
wake_on_request.note: Pause/resume is unimplemented (501); there is no sleep/wake lifecycle — a sandbox only goes create -> running -> stopped.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Commands do not reset the deadline. This is not an idle timer.
auto_stop_idle.note: Sandboxes stop only at a fixed timeoutMs deadline set at creation (or via setTimeout), or an explicit kill; there is no idle-based auto-stop.

live_resize.quote: Current sandboxes use fixed limits of 4 vCPU and 4096 MiB RAM. Create options do not change these limits.
live_resize.note: CPU/RAM are fixed for the sandbox's lifetime; no resize API exists.

agent_harnesses.quote: Enabled templates include `base`, `codex`, and `interpreter`; availability depends on the region and pool capacity.
agent_harnesses.note: A `codex` sandbox template is offered as a preinstalled catalog option (Codex CLI harness).

own_agent_api.quote: Lizard deploys your apps from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other AI coding agents in one command — build, run, and manage services alongside managed Postgres, Redis, and S3 object storage.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Lizard is driven BY external coding agents/CLIs; it does not offer its own first-party browser/computer-use/research task-agent API.

mcp_server.quote: Lizard Skill uses Lizard CLI. That workflow does not expose an MCP transport. Hosting your own remote MCP server is a separate application deployment.
mcp_server.note: The provider does maintain a separate open-source MCP server (github.com/lizard-build/lizard-mcp) with tools for services/deploys/logs/secrets/domains/volumes, but it has no sandbox create/exec/list tools — it does not control sandboxes specifically.

public_ipv4.quote: Start a server that listens on `0.0.0.0`, then call `getHost(port)` to register its public HTTPS hostname.
public_ipv4.note: Exposure is via a generated public HTTPS hostname, not a per-machine public IPv4 address; no public IPv4 feature is documented.

ingress_rules.quote: The port is public; add authentication if the server needs it.
ingress_rules.note: Exposed ports are plain public HTTPS hostnames; no provider-side IP allowlist, private/auth URL, or security-group control is documented for sandboxes.

egress_allowlist.quote: Sandboxes run short-lived commands and agent tasks in Kubernetes pods with the runc runtime. They share the host kernel; they are not Firecracker virtual machines. Restrict credentials and network access when running code you do not trust.
egress_allowlist.note: Docs tell the customer to restrict network access themselves; no provider-side egress allow/deny-list or no-internet mode is documented across sandbox/limits/known-issues pages.

egress_http_rules.quote: Restrict credentials and network access when running code you do not trust.
egress_http_rules.note: No HTTP method/path-level egress control is documented; even the coarser egress_allowlist feature is absent.

static_egress_ip.quote: Sandboxes run short-lived commands and agent tasks in Kubernetes pods with the runc runtime.
static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/static outbound IP feature is documented; sandboxes run on shared Kubernetes nodes.

gpu.quote: CPU $0.000006948 per vCPU/s Memory $0.000003474 per GB/s Volumes $0.000000054 per GB/s Managed Object Storage $0.0135 per GB/month Egress $0.045 per GB
gpu.note: not offered: the full published rate card has no GPU line item and no GPU machine type is mentioned anywhere in the docs.

windows.quote: Sandboxes run short-lived commands and agent tasks in Kubernetes pods with the runc runtime.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — only Linux container templates (base, codex, interpreter) exist; no Windows machine option.

macos.quote: Sandboxes run short-lived commands and agent tasks in Kubernetes pods with the runc runtime.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Linux Kubernetes pods only; no macOS machine option.

self_host.quote: Cloud pricing for the way AI agents work Pay as you go for CPU, memory, storage and egress with no monthly subscription.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Lizard is a hosted multi-tenant cloud platform (Kubernetes clusters it operates); no self-hosted/on-prem distribution is offered, unlike the MIT/Apache-licensed CLI/SDK client tools.

byoc.quote: Everything in Pro Custom replica limits SOC 2 & HIPAA compliance SSO / SAML RBAC & audit log Dedicated, hands-on support with SLAs Dedicated nodes on demand
byoc.note: Enterprise offers dedicated nodes within Lizard's own infrastructure, not deployment of the managed service into the customer's own cloud account; no BYOC option documented.

open_source.quote: lizard-cli (MIT), skill (MIT), lizard-sdk (Apache-2.0), lizard-studio (MIT), lizard-mcp (MIT) are public repos; the hosted sandbox/compute platform itself is not among them.
open_source.note: The CLI, SDK, editor skill, MCP server, and Studio browser extension are open source, but the core hosted sandbox/compute platform (the product being scored) is closed-source.

soc2.quote: Everything in Pro Custom replica limits SOC 2 & HIPAA compliance SSO / SAML RBAC & audit log Dedicated, hands-on support with SLAs Dedicated nodes on demand

hipaa.quote: Everything in Pro Custom replica limits SOC 2 & HIPAA compliance SSO / SAML RBAC & audit log Dedicated, hands-on support with SLAs Dedicated nodes on demand

eu_data_residency.quote: The current configured regions include US East (Virginia), `us-east-1`, and EU West (Limburg), `eu-west-lim-a`.
eu_data_residency.note: An EU region (Limburg, Netherlands) is selectable for sandboxes and apps.

max_session_h.quote: The SDK and CLI default to a five-minute lifetime. The raw API and dashboard default to no expiration. Set an explicit lifetime: `timeoutMs: 0` at creation disables expiration.
max_session_h.note: No provider-enforced maximum: dashboard-created and raw-API sandboxes have no expiration unless the caller sets one; the caller-settable explicit lifetime cap is ~2147483647 ms (~596.5 h), but that is an optional self-imposed timer, not a forced platform ceiling.

persistent_disk.quote: A volume in Lizard (lizard.build) keeps data after a sandbox stops. It mounts at **`/workspace`** and attaches to **one sandbox at a time**. ... Killing or expiring a sandbox detaches its volume and keeps the data.
persistent_disk.note: Card's own contradiction is right to flag persistent_disk=false, but the mechanism is a Persistent Volume, not pause/resume (pause/resume/snapshot/fork/restore all return HTTP 501 per docs, so those are NOT the basis). Default (no volume attached) is non-persistent: '/workspace is temporary' without one. Opt in by attaching a named Volume at create time; then files at /workspace survive kill/expiration and can be reused by a later sandbox.

snapshot.quote: Pause, resume, fork, snapshot, restore, and file watching currently return HTTP 501.
snapshot.note: No snapshot capability of any kind (auto or on-demand) is offered; confirmed by explicit 501 on the snapshot/restore endpoints, consistent with card's feature_evidence for snapshot_auto/snapshot_on_demand.

custom_image.quote: Choose a template from the current catalog. Enabled templates include `base`, `codex`, and `interpreter`; availability depends on the region and pool capacity. ... The public CLI does not provide a custom-template upload flow.
custom_image.note: Only a fixed catalog of pre-built templates is selectable; there is no way for a customer to bring or build their own image/template.

image_oci.quote: The public CLI does not provide a custom-template upload flow.
image_oci.note: No mention anywhere in docs/llms.txt of accepting an OCI/Docker image as a sandbox source; sandboxes run on Kubernetes/runc from a closed template catalog only (base/codex/interpreter), so OCI-image-based sandbox creation is not offered.
